summary: In commercial and defense launch activity, Rocket Lab successfully launched three Hawk signals intelligence satellites into orbit, while navigation startup Xona raised $250 million in Series D funding to scale its commercial GPS constellation. On the defense front, the U.S. Space Force selected six companies for its Commercial Reserve Fleet and announced plans to issue requests for information regarding cislunar warfare, while Ukraine revealed plans to establish an independent satellite communications network alongside ICEYE and Nokia following Starshield service interruptions. Additionally, DARPA awarded Space Nuclear Power Corporation an agreement to conduct a ground test of an autonomous nuclear reactor controller. In civil space developments, Europe's re-entry technology faced a setback as the Space Rider vehicle crashed during a drop test, while a new National Academies report ranked potential nonpolar lunar landing sites, and NASA completed another RS-25 engine test in support of its Artemis program. In astronomical science, NASA's Hubble Space Telescope mapped gravitational lenses to assist the upcoming Roman Space Telescope, the James Webb Space Telescope captured images of stars forming in a stellar nursery, and reanalyzed Viking 2 data revealed evidence of a historic marsquake. Readers should watch for a live NASA update on October 23 regarding the agency's Artemis moon plans.
